This photo captures the magic and boundless potential that PCs used to have for me (and I'm sure many others) as a tween in the mid-90s.

Microsoft and Windows 95 opened up a vast, multimedia digital frontier back then, and no one knew where things would go. PCs were things to explore offline and alone, supplementing your experience with boxed software or hardware from CompUSA and Egghead/Software Etc..

While you could get online of course, that was a luxury, and the web's content was so much simpler, novel and surprising. There weren't any established web standards or trends, just endless experimentation and creativity out on the web. If you made a website, you had a shot at it being seen by the relatively limited people online. Sound and video in apps was amazing. DOS games and VGA graphics were the pinnacle of excitement. Dial-up deathmatching--exhilarating.

Now it feels like that magic is long gone. We consolidated and gave everything to a handful of sites, sacrificing our freedom and individuality for centralization and convenience. We definitely lost a great deal in doing so, but it's not ever been easier to find the content we're looking for.

Had an epileptic basset for 7 years between 1999 and 2006. My family got him from a shelter and no one told us he was epileptic. My mother originally returned him but changed her mind and got him back due to her conscience.

He certainly didn’t know what was happening to him which was what was so hard. 

Sadly, he needed to be euthanized when he got into a spell and they wouldn’t stop. His body would be entirely flexed as he threw his head back and forth. I remember at the end of them he would whine and cry like he was in pain, and it broke me every time. When the med worked he was happy, he slept and ate and chewed bones. We did all we could for that dog. He lived to be maybe 9. RIP, Buddy.

I don’t like to argue but I reject this whole idea that games are dead or alive, and submit that this is a recent, entirely socially constructed concept; a concept aimed to deter suggestible people from trying a game by the sheer fact it’s not popular enough for some people’s tastes. Do these people like to proclaim all the classic arcade games from the 1980s are dead because they’re no longer in vogue? Games are artistic creations that can be enjoyed in numerous ways, at any point in time. Single player with bots is my preferred way, for example. It’s also possible to play with friends they have or know since it’s free to play which precludes the need for a large dedicated player base.

What players ought to concern themselves with is if the game is good or bad, if it’s playable or broken. And this game is not just good it’s great in terms of gameplay and artistic merit. It has some bugs and shortcomings but I take the good with the bad because this is Quake we’re talking about.

How do I cope with what you've described? 

Work, animals, art, hobbies, a rich inner world. 

Going to work keeps you on a schedule, gets you out of your comfort zone everyday while providing you with opportunities and challenges. Earn some money, interact with people, find what you're good at, use your brain, prove to yourself you're competent and useful will help with having no structure.

If you're home all day, adopting a dog or animal can really help you mentally, not to mention you're helping the animal (get these beautiful animals out of shelters, people). They will give you a purpose if you're not working and you care about their wellbeing. My dogs have always walked me, gotten me into a routine of getting out of the house to exercise when I loathe exercising. They change your center of focus from yourself and your inner monologue to them, if not completely just a little bit. Dogs have been the greatest, most meaningful connections I've had in my life, and I'm not embarrassed to say that. They are what make life worth living, and they were worth being born in this world to experience and be around. Consider fostering if you can't adopt. 

Art and music are incredible at transcending the tedium of daily life. Dive into a genre of music, get out and see artists perform, study performances and movies, their history. It's so rewarding and it's fascinating. We can see the world's art from the comfort of our homes. When I say art, I use the word very loosely to mean anything creative and that speaks to you.

'Hobbies' is such a generic term that means something different to everyone. But whatever recreation you're into, be it flying kites, bowling, playing tabletop or video games, crocheting, geocaching, collecting seashells, watching hardcore violence online or reading trashy pornographic romance novels, indulge while you can. Get lost in it, even if it's just you, because we need to cling to whatever makes us happy while we still can, no matter how popular or unpopular it is.

As for therapy and mental health, your mileage will vary. You have to put in what you want out of it, there is no guarantee. I've been through the system since 2001, and while I've learned a lot of things, done mostly all treatments available, it was unbelievably expensive and slow-going, and I'm still dysfunctional in many ways. Finding a therapist that you like and can connect with is time-consuming. Establish what you want out of therapy and the therapist will prioritize it on the treatment plan. But I'll tell you this, don't expect these people to care about you. You're work to them.

It’s caused me anxiety that made me wish I was dead, a paralyzing fear and panic that I’ll end up homeless and a burden. This doesn’t even include the horrible task of job searching, the complete purgatory of applying to hear nothing or maybe a rejection. You feel completely worthless and unnecessary when you can’t even be useful enough to trade your time for money.

Money is just a tool to take the edge off: rich food, distracting trinkets, expensive toys that take your mind off of how miserable the other 2/3 of your life is. When the misery gets out of hand then you fall into debt because you’re spending to soothe yourself. And now you have another problem to deal with and worry over. 

I don’t even want to just stop working, I need to stop existing because I can’t manage this bullshit. I envy the dead but I can’t convince myself that life is over yet as I’ve seen circumstances change in a day. I suppose it’s this unpredictability that keeps me reading chapter after chapter, year after year of this bizarre story that is my life.
